# Profinity 2.3 documentation, full page list

> Every page of the Profinity 2.3 documentation with a one-line description. Generated from page front matter by scripts/generate-llms-txt.js. For a short index, see /llms.txt.

## Getting Started

- [Getting started with Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Getting_Started/index.html): Start here to install Profinity, create a user, load a profile, add components and see your data on a dashboard.
- [Create a user](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Getting_Started/Create_User.html): Create a Profinity user, set an initial password and assign roles so the person can sign in with the access they need.
- [Profinity profiles](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Getting_Started/Profiles.html): Understand how a Profinity profile keeps the configuration of your system, and where to activate, add, and upload profiles.
- [Quick start guide](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Getting_Started/Quick_Start.html): Install Profinity 2.3 on Windows, apply a licence, load an example profile, replay CAN logs, edit your first dashboard and look at rules and alerts.

## Installation

- [Installing Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/index.html): Choose how to install Profinity on Windows, Linux, macOS, or Docker, then apply a licence, set environment variables and run it as a service.
- [Run Profinity as a service](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Run_as_a_Service/index.html): Choose how to run Profinity as a service on Linux, macOS, or Windows so it starts automatically on boot, and check the licence that remote access needs.
- [Apply a licence](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Applying_a_Licence.html): Apply a Profinity licence file after installation, from the License page or by copying it into the licence folder, and check that it has taken effect.
- [Artefacts directory](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Artifacts_Directory.html): Find where Profinity stores configuration, profiles, plugins, and logs on Windows, macOS, and Linux, and how to move it with PROFINITY_HOME.
- [Install Profinity with Docker](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Docker_Installation.html): Install and run Profinity in a Docker container with Docker Compose, sign in, expose CAN devices, and prepare the installation for production.
- [Install Profinity with the Docker one-line installer](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Docker_One_Line_Installer.html): Install Profinity in Docker with the install-docker.sh script, which writes the compose file, pulls the image, and starts Profinity.
- [Environment variables](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Environment_Variables.html): Set Profinity configuration and profile values from environment variables with the ${VARIABLE_NAME} placeholder, and see the variables Profinity reads.
- [Install Profinity from an archive](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Linux_and_macOS_Archive_Installation.html): Install Profinity on Linux or macOS from a downloaded archive without an installer, choose the archive for your processor, and start it with profinity.sh.
- [Install Profinity on Linux and macOS](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Linux_and_macOS_Installation.html): Install Profinity on Linux and macOS with the bootstrap installer, update it, find where it stores data, open the web interface, and sign in.
- [Migrate from Profinity V1 to V2](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Migration.html): Move from Profinity V1 to V2 with a clean installation, because the two versions are not compatible and there is no downgrade path.
- [Run Profinity as a Linux service](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Run_as_a_Service/Run_as_a_Linux_Service.html): Run Profinity as a systemd service on Linux so it starts on boot and restarts on failure, with the unit file, start commands and troubleshooting.
- [Run Profinity as a macOS service](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Run_as_a_Service/Run_as_a_macOS_Service.html): Run Profinity as a launchd service on macOS so it starts automatically at boot and restarts if it stops, with the plist, load commands and checks.
- [Run Profinity as a Windows service](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Run_as_a_Service/Run_as_a_Windows_Service.html): Run Profinity as a Windows service with ProfinityService.cmd, choose the account it runs under, set the data folder, and remove the service.
- [Security guide](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Security.html): Implement essential security controls for Profinity production deployments including HTTPS, user accounts, scripting, and kiosk mode.
- [Update the Profinity Docker image](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Update_Docker_Image.html): Move a Docker installation to a newer Profinity image with Docker Compose, or update it automatically each day with Watchtower.
- [Upgrade from Profinity 2.2](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Upgrade_From_2_2.html): Upgrade a Profinity 2.2 installation to 2.3 in order: back up, install, check the licence, roles, dashboards, firmware passcodes, and integrations.
- [Install Profinity on Windows](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Installation/Windows_Installation.html): Install Profinity on Windows with the Setup Wizard, open the web interface in a browser, and see what needs a Server licence.

## Administration

- [Administering Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/index.html): Administer a running Profinity: system settings, users, and roles, profiles, licensing, logs, and the plugins and component types engineers can use.
- [System Configuration](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/index.html): Find the System Configuration tab for application, logging, discovery, web, extensions web, tags, security, and AI settings.
- [Security](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Security/index.html): Find the System Configuration Security tab pages for sign-in, passwords, two-factor, SCIM, and SIEM, and set session lifetime and login lockout.
- [Users and access](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/index.html): Manage who can sign in to Profinity and what they can do: user accounts, roles, service accounts, multi-factor authentication, and security restrictions.
- [Choose available components](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Choose_Available_Components.html): Hide or show component types, or whole groups, in the Add Component list from the component catalogue on the Components & Plugins page.
- [Feedback](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Feedback.html): Send suggestions, issue reports and comments to Prohelion from the built-in Feedback form on the ADMIN page.
- [Install and manage plugins](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Install_and_Manage_Plugins.html): Upload, enable, disable, and delete plugins on the Components & Plugins page, and find where Profinity stores installed plugins.
- [Kiosk Mode](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Kiosk_Mode.html): Set up automatic sign-in for kiosk displays and unattended monitoring stations, bypassing the login page for a specific profile.
- [License manager](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/License_Manager.html): Read the licence state, type, edition, expiry, fingerprint, and licensed features of a Profinity instance on the License page under ADMIN.
- [Logs](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Logs_Config.html): View Profinity system logs from the ADMIN page and find where the recorded log level, rollover size and retention are set.
- [Menu Layout](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Menu_Layout.html): Arrange the components and groups in the top section of the side menu, including group names, icons, and order, using the Menu Layout editor.
- [Profile Dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Profile_Dashboard.html): Create a custom home page dashboard for a profile in the visual editor or from a YAML file, and remove it again.
- [Profiles](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Profiles.html): Create, activate, rename, import, and download profiles that hold your device configurations, with Kiosk Mode and custom dashboard options.
- [Profinity AI settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/AI_Settings.html): Set the provider, model, API key, web search and timeout for the instance-wide Profinity AI assistant, and see what data leaves the instance.
- [Application Config](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Application_Config.html): Set packet retention, update checks, the recent tag history window and scripting on the System Configuration Application Config tab.
- [Discovery](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Discovery.html): Configure the LAN heartbeat that lets Profinity Mobile find this Profinity server, including its name, UDP port and interval.
- [Extensions Web](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Extensions_Web.html): Configure the second web server that hosts custom applications and the Profinity API, with its ports, API, and Swagger options.
- [Logging](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Logging.html): Set the log level, log rollover size and number of retained logs on the System Configuration Logging tab.
- [Profinity Web](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Profinity_Web.html): Set the HTTP and HTTPS addresses and ports of the main Profinity web server, choose its certificates, and fix remote access problems.
- [Password policy](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Security/Password_Policy.html): Set password length, complexity, and expiry rules for local sign-in, force password changes and let users change their own password.
- [SCIM and SIEM](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Security/SCIM_and_SIEM.html): Enable SCIM user provisioning from identity providers and configure SIEM export of security audit events, including the event line format.
- [SSO and sign-in method](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Security/SSO_and_Sign_In.html): Choose the site-wide sign-in method, configure OpenID Connect single sign-on, link users to accounts and recover from a misconfigured provider.
- [Two-factor authentication](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Security/Two_Factor_Authentication.html): Require time-based one-time password (TOTP) two-factor authentication for local users, set recovery code and device trust policy, and allow security keys.
- [Tags](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Configuration/Tags.html): Set the limits on the in-memory tag history buffer, including points per tag, total points and time to live, on the Tags tab.
- [System Information](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/System_Info.html): View the Profinity version, licence status, active memory, uptime, and release history, and restart Profinity from the ADMIN page.
- [Component and collection security](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/Component_And_Collection_Security.html): Control which users can see profile components and tag collections through role-based security restrictions.
- [Managing users](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/Manage_Users.html): Create user accounts, give each person the roles they need, and find the password and two-factor settings that apply to them.
- [MFA account management](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/MFA_Account_Management.html): Reset a user's multi-factor authentication or password as an administrator, and manage your own authenticator from the ADMIN page.
- [Roles and permissions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/Roles_and_Permissions.html): Control what each person can see and do in Profinity by creating roles, assigning them to users, and finding every permission.
- [Service accounts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Administration/Users_and_Access/Service_Accounts.html): Create service accounts with API tokens that never expire, for automation and external Model Context Protocol (MCP) client access.

## Components

- [Battery management systems](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Battery_Management_Systems/index.html): Find the page for adding a Prohelion BMU to a profile, reading the BMU dashboard, changing firmware settings and flashing BMU firmware.
- [CAN bus adapters](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/CAN_Bus_Protocols/index.html): Connect Profinity to a CAN bus with a CAN to Ethernet bridge, Peak USB, SocketCAN, SocketCANd, or Ewert CANdapter, or relay traffic with a virtual adapter.
- [Chargers and power supplies](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Chargers_and_Power/index.html): Find the page for adding a TDK, Siglent, or Elcon charger to a profile, setting its limits, starting a battery charge and fixing charging faults.
- [Historians](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Historians/index.html): Choose a historian to store tag history in InfluxDB v2, InfluxDB v3 or a SQL database, and set which one answers long-range history queries.
- [Industrial protocols](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/index.html): Find the Profinity plugin for BACnet, EtherNet/IP, Modbus, OPC UA or S7, and what you need to install and licence it before you add its components.
- [Loggers](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/index.html): Choose a Profinity logger to write tag collections or CAN messages to files, an SFTP server, InfluxDB v1 or Prometheus.
- [Motor controllers](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Motor_Controller/index.html): Find the page for adding a WaveSculptor motor controller to a profile, reading its dashboard, and configuring it or flashing its firmware.
- [Publishers and Subscribers](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Publishers_and_Subscribers/index.html): Choose a publisher or subscriber to move tag values between Profinity and MQTT brokers, web services or Sparkplug B sources, or use a logger or Tag Relay.
- [Tag Relays](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Tag_Relays/index.html): Share live tags between Profinity instances with a Tag Relay Sender and a Tag Relay Receiver, over HTTPS or MQTT.
- [BMU dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Battery_Management_Systems/BMU_Dashboard.html): Read the Prohelion BMU dashboard: the summary row, status indicators, BMU state machine flowchart and the Node Telemetry table of CMU cell voltages.
- [Prohelion BMU](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Battery_Management_Systems/Prohelion_BMU.html): Add a Prohelion Battery Management Unit to a profile, choose the BMS model and set its base address, timeout, and Control Pack option.
- [Update BMU configuration and firmware](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Battery_Management_Systems/Update_BMU_Configuration_and_Firmware.html): Change the firmware configuration of a Prohelion BMU, unlock the Admin firmware parameters with a session key, and flash the BMU firmware.
- [CAN bus adapter settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/CAN_Bus_Protocols/CAN_Bus_Adapter_Settings.html): Look up the parameters and defaults for each CAN bus adapter: Tritium CAN to Ethernet bridge, SocketCANd, Peak, CANdapter, and native SocketCAN.
- [CAN bus adapter troubleshooting](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/CAN_Bus_Protocols/CAN_Bus_Adapter_Troubleshooting.html): Fix a CAN bus adapter with an amber or red status, a missing Peak driver, a CAN to Ethernet bridge Auto Discovery does not find, or a bit rate mismatch.
- [CAN bus adapters](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/CAN_Bus_Protocols/CAN_Bus_Adapters.html): Choose a CAN bus adapter, such as a Prohelion or Tritium CAN to Ethernet bridge, a Peak USB adapter, or SocketCAN, and add it with Auto Discovery.
- [Prohelion Virtual CAN Bus Adapter](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/CAN_Bus_Protocols/Virtual_CAN_Adapter.html): Add a Virtual CAN Bridge that relays CAN traffic between Profinity adapters and bridge clients over TCP or UDP, with V1 and V2 protocol support.
- [Charger components](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Chargers_and_Power/Charger_Components.html): Choose a TDK Power Supply, Siglent Power Supply or Elcon Charger component and add it to a profile with a Prohelion BMS to charge a battery pack.
- [Charger settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Chargers_and_Power/Charger_Settings.html): Look up the voltage, current, and power limits, network, and CAN settings of the TDK Power Supply, Siglent Power Supply and Elcon Charger components.
- [Charging troubleshooting](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Chargers_and_Power/Charging_Troubleshooting.html): Fix a charge that does not start or a pack that does not engage, using the charger controller messages, the status lamps and the precharge checks.
- [Start a charge](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Chargers_and_Power/Start_a_Charge.html): Start and stop a battery charge from the charger dashboard by selecting the battery, setting the charge current and Charge To level, and pressing START.
- [Prohelion Cloud Dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Cloud_Dashboard/Prohelion_Cloud_Dashboard.html): Send Profinity tag values to the Prohelion Cloud platform with the Prohelion Cloud Dashboard component, including settings, licensing, and network requirements.
- [Connections and reconnecting](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Connections_and_Reconnecting.html): How components that connect to a broker, device, server, or database start, show a problem, and recover, with retry timing and the Off, On, and Error status.
- [Using a Custom Component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Custom_Components/Using_a_Custom_Component.html): Use a Custom Component in a profile, with an optional DBC file, dashboard, and scripts.
- [Dashboard Component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Dashboard/Dashboard_Component.html): Add a built-in profile component that renders a YAML dashboard bound to existing tags, with no DBC file, and learn how to bind tags with absolute paths.
- [InfluxDB historians](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Historians/InfluxDB_Historians.html): Record tag history to an InfluxDB v2 or v3 server and read it back through the APIs, with setup, settings, and log messages that explain a failed connection.
- [TAG SQL Historian](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Historians/TAG_SQL_Historian.html): Record tag history to a SQLite, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or Oracle table, read it back through the APIs, and find the table layout and connection strings.
- [BACnet](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/BACnet.html): Configure the BACnet Device component to poll BACnet/IP object present-values from a building automation device into Profinity tags.
- [EtherNet/IP](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/EtherNet_IP.html): Configure the EtherNet/IP PLC component to poll Allen-Bradley CIP tags into Profinity tags, with CIP path, PLC kind and data type settings.
- [Modbus](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/Modbus.html): Configure the Modbus Device component to poll coils and registers from a Modbus TCP or RTU slave into Profinity tags, with point map and scaling.
- [OPC UA certificates](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/OPC_UA_Certificates.html): Find where the OPC UA Client and OPC UA Server keep their application certificates on each platform, and how to trust a certificate explicitly.
- [OPC UA Client](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/OPC_UA_Client.html): Poll the nodes of a remote OPC UA server into Profinity tags, with a point map of NodeIds, optional user name and password, and certificate trust settings.
- [OPC UA Server](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/OPC_UA_Server.html): Expose the readable scalar tags of a Profinity profile to third-party OPC UA clients as a read-only address space, and set the address the server listens on.
- [S7](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Industrial_Protocols/S7.html): Configure the S7 PLC component to poll Siemens S7 data blocks, memory, inputs, and outputs into Profinity tags, and prepare the PLC for access.
- [CAN file and SFTP loggers](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/CAN_File_and_SFTP_Loggers.html): Record native CAN bus messages to a text file on the Profinity machine or send them to a remote SFTP server, and choose the Prohelion or Tritium file format.
- [File logger rotation, archive, and SFTP settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/File_Logger_Rotation_Archive_and_SFTP.html): Look up the SFTP connection settings and the rotation, archive, compression, and file limit settings shared by the CAN and TAG file and SFTP loggers.
- [InfluxDB v1 Logger](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/InfluxDB_v1_Logger.html): Log selected tag collections to an InfluxDB v1 server, with the settings, the health check option for InfluxDB Cloud, and what to check if no data arrives.
- [Prometheus Logger](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/Prometheus_Logger.html): Serve selected tag collections to a Prometheus server, with the endpoint settings, the default data URL, and what to check if Prometheus shows no data.
- [Tag file and SFTP loggers](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Loggers/Tag_File_and_SFTP_Loggers.html): Log selected tag collections to local CSV or JSON Lines files, or send them to a remote SFTP server, with logging mode, interval, and file format settings.
- [Logging modes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Logging_Modes.html): What the Snapshot, On Change and Everything logging modes send, how the update interval applies in each, and where the default interval differs.
- [Update WaveSculptor configuration and firmware](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Motor_Controller/Update_WaveSculptor_Configuration_and_Firmware.html): Configure a WaveSculptor with wsConfig from the Setup and Config button and flash its firmware, using a Windows desktop instance and a CAN to Ethernet bridge.
- [WaveSculptor dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Motor_Controller/WaveSculptor_Dashboard.html): Read the WaveSculptor dashboard: bus voltage, current, and power, temperatures, speed, and the controller limit and error indicators.
- [WaveSculptor motor controller](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Motor_Controller/WaveSculptor.html): Add a Prohelion WaveSculptor22 or WaveSculptor200 motor controller to a profile and set its name, timeout, and CAN base address.
- [Elmar Solar MPPT](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/MPPT/Elmar_Solar_MPPT.html): Monitor an Elmar Solar maximum power point tracker in Profinity: add it to a profile, then read its input and output voltage, power graphs and status events.
- [MQTT Publisher](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Publishers_and_Subscribers/MQTT_Publisher.html): Publish profile tag collections to MQTT brokers in JSON or Sparkplug B format on interval or change.
- [MQTT Subscriber](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Publishers_and_Subscribers/MQTT_Subscriber.html): Subscribe to an external Sparkplug B source over MQTT and write its metrics into the profile tag tree as read-only tags.
- [Webhook Publisher](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Publishers_and_Subscribers/Webhook_Publisher.html): Push profile tag collections to an HTTP or HTTPS endpoint with a POST and a JSON payload, on an interval or when a value changes.
- [Set up a tag relay](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Tag_Relays/Set_Up_a_Tag_Relay.html): Set up a first Tag Relay between two Profinity instances over HTTPS or MQTT, from the tag collection on the sender to the relayed tags on the receiver.
- [Tag Relay Receiver](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Tag_Relays/Tag_Relay_Receiver.html): Receive tags from remote Profinity instances over MQTT or HTTPS and mount them as read-only tags under a per-site prefix.
- [Tag Relay Sender](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Components/Tag_Relays/Tag_Relay_Sender.html): Publish a snapshot of selected tag collections to a remote Profinity instance over HTTPS or MQTT at a fixed interval.

## Tags

- [Tag collections](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Collections/index.html): Group tags for filtering, dashboards, and rules using the visual editor and membership expressions.
- [Derived tags](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Derived_Tags/index.html): Virtual tags computed automatically from expressions or scripts that behave like real tags, with a worked example and a guide to choosing between them.
- [Tag layer](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/index.html): Find the page for browsing tags, grouping them into collections, alerting on them, logging, replaying, and relaying them between Profinity instances.
- [Rule actions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/Actions/index.html): Choose actions for a tag rule, add Email, Slack, Webhook, MQTT, and script actions, and see how actions are inherited and which message placeholders exist.
- [Tag rules](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/index.html): Write tag rules in rules.yaml or the visual editor, set alert levels and thresholds, and attach actions that run when a rule fires.
- [Selecting tags](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Selecting_Tags/index.html): Find the pages on tag tree paths, nesting a component in the tree, and the expression language that collections, rules, and derived tags use to pick tags.
- [Tag logs](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Tag_Logs/index.html): Find the pages for recording tag values to a log file and replaying that log back onto live tags, for testing rules, alerts, and dashboards.
- [Alerts Log](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Alerts.html): View, acknowledge, and silence rule-generated alerts in the Alerts Log, with active and history tabs and live alert indicators.
- [Create a collection](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Collections/Create_a_Collection.html): Create a group and a restricted collection of cell voltages in the collections editor, using a scope, a membership expression, and role-based security.
- [Create collections, rules, and dashboard bindings from tags](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Create_Collections_Rules_and_Bindings_from_Tags.html): Right-click tags in Tag Explorer to create collections, rules, and dashboard bindings from the selection, without copying it into the editors by hand.
- [Create a derived tag with a script](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Derived_Tags/Create_a_Derived_Tag_with_a_Script.html): Compute derived tags with a script when one expression is not enough, including multi-step logic, state, and several output tags.
- [Create a derived tag](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Derived_Tags/Create_a_Derived_Tag.html): Create an expression-based derived tag that converts speed from mph to km/h, grouped under a vehicle, in the derived tags editor.
- [Email and Slack rule actions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/Actions/Email_and_Slack_Rule_Actions.html): Configure the Email Rule Action and Slack Rule Action settings, including the SMTP server, recipients, Slack webhook URL, channel, and message templates.
- [Webhook and MQTT rule actions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/Actions/Webhook_and_MQTT_Rule_Actions.html): Send rule notifications to an HTTP endpoint or an MQTT broker, with the JSON message format, a guide to choosing between them, and the action settings.
- [Create a rule](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/Create_a_Rule.html): Create a threshold rule in the rules visual editor that raises a Warning and then a Fatal alert as a battery pack temperature rises.
- [Complete rules.yaml example](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Rules/Rules_YAML_Example.html): Read a complete rules.yaml with file and group actions, a threshold rule with dwell and deadband, and a boolean rule that uses a collection.
- [Nest a component in the tag tree](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Selecting_Tags/Nest_a_Component_in_the_Tag_Tree.html): Set the Tag tree path of a component so its tags mount inside a parent folder, resolve overlapping paths, and change the path of a deployed component safely.
- [Tag expressions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Selecting_Tags/Tag_Expressions.html): Look up the expression language that collections, rules, and derived tags use to select tags, compare values and compute derived values.
- [Tag tree paths and dashboard binds](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Selecting_Tags/Tag_Tree_Path.html): Learn how the Tag tree path setting nests a component in the tag tree, and how nesting affects scopes and dashboard binds.
- [Log tags to a file](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Tag_Logs/Log_Tags_to_a_File.html): Record tag values to a CSV or JSON Lines file with the TAG File Logger or TAG SFTP Logger so that the recording can be replayed later.
- [Replay a tag log](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Tag_Logs/Replay_a_Tag_Log.html): Play a recorded tag log back onto your live tags with TAG LOG REPLAY, using the pause, stop, and loop controls, and learn what replay does to your tags.
- [Tag relay](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Tags/Tag_Relay.html): Share live tags between Profinity instances using sender and receiver roles, a choice of HTTPS or MQTT transport, and per-site tag prefixes.

## Customising Profinity

- [Component reference](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/index.html): Reference for the dashboard components in four categories: layout, data display, content, and interactive.
- [Data binding](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Data_Binding/index.html): Learn how a dashboard binding names a tag by path, which tags a dashboard can use, and the instant, time series and logged binding modes.
- [Profinity dashboard development guide](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/index.html): View a component's dashboard, and find the pages for building dashboards in the visual editor, binding them to tags, and working with the YAML format.
- [Hosting custom applications](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Hosting/index.html): Host a custom web application from Profinity's integrated web server and secure it with HTTPS certificates for production use.
- [Customising Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/index.html): Tailor how Profinity looks and behaves for a deployment with dashboards, theming, hosted web applications, and OEM white-label mobile builds.
- [Themes and branding](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Theming/index.html): Apply your own colours, logos, and application title to the Profinity web client with a theme.yaml file in the themes folder.
- [HTML component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Content/HTML.html): Embed custom HTML content with references to profile assets for rich text formatting and custom layouts, or show a map that follows a position.
- [Icon component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Content/Icon.html): Display an icon from the Carbon icon set or the profile images directory.
- [Redirect component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Content/Redirect.html): Immediately navigates to another page or address when the dashboard displays the component.
- [Caption component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Caption.html): Show a line of text on a dashboard from a static string or a bound value, such as a status message or mapped text.
- [Charts component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Charts.html): Data visualisation component supporting line, bar, radar, pie, doughnut, bubble, scatter, and polar area charts.
- [Lamp component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Lamp.html): Single colour-coded status indicator with a label, driven by a value, an enabled state and a colour.
- [Lamps component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Lamps.html): Grid of colour-coded status indicators for quick system state visualisation and error/warning displays.
- [Readouts component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Readouts.html): Display numerical and text values with units, precision control, and data binding for sensor readings and measurements.
- [State component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/State.html): State machine visualisation component using Mermaid flowcharts to display system states and transitions.
- [Tables component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Data/Tables.html): Data table display with heatmap visualisation, highlighting, and value threshold alerts for multi-dimensional data.
- [Image component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Images_and_Models/Image.html): Place clickable regions, icons, buttons, live data values, points, and annotation lines on a base image in a dashboard.
- [3D model component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Images_and_Models/Model.html): Show a 3D model that operators orbit and zoom, with clickable regions, icons, buttons, live data values and annotation lines in model space.
- [Overlay elements](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Images_and_Models/Overlay_Elements.html): Reference for the action invocation, layers, icon sources, display types and annotation lines that the Image and 3D model components share.
- [Actions component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Interactive/Actions.html): Add a button or icon that runs a component or system action, navigates to a location, or sends an HTTP request from a dashboard.
- [Tabs component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Interactive/Tabs.html): Organise several data views into tabs whose headers carry a status lamp and caption, with panels as the body of each tab.
- [Toggles component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Interactive/Toggles.html): Add an on/off switch that runs an action when clicked and shows whether a feature is on or off from bound data.
- [Accordion component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Accordion.html): Reference for the Accordion dashboard component: its parameters, defaults, and examples for collapsible sections, binding, and nesting.
- [Footer component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Footer.html): Reference for the Footer dashboard component: the bar at the bottom of a dashboard, its parameters and how to show or hide it with a binding.
- [Group component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Group.html): Reference for the Group dashboard component: a container that arranges related components horizontally or vertically, with its parameters and examples.
- [Panel component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Panel.html): Reference for the Panel dashboard component: a titled container inside a panels grid, with its parameters, sizing options and examples.
- [Panels component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Panels.html): Reference for the Panels dashboard component: a grid of panel containers, with its parameters, height options and an example.
- [Pill component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Pill.html): Reference for the Pill dashboard component: a compact status display with an icon and grouped values, with its parameters and an example.
- [Row component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Row.html): Reference for the Row dashboard component: a layout container that arranges components vertically or horizontally, with its parameters and an example.
- [Titlebar component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Component_Reference/Layout/Titlebar.html): Reference for the Titlebar dashboard component: the header bar with a status lamp and menu toolbar, with its parameters, menu item behaviour and an example.
- [Core elements](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Core_Elements.html): Learn the four top-level elements of a dashboard (titlebar, row, accordion, footer), how items nest, and how rows lay out their contents.
- [Binding settings reference](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Data_Binding/Binding_Settings_Reference.html): Look up every setting a dashboard binding accepts, grouped by what it does, with its type, default, and the page that explains it.
- [Conditional styling](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Data_Binding/Conditional_Styling.html): Change a dashboard component's visibility, colour, label, or enabled state from a live tag value with data binding targets and value mapping.
- [Transform and map values](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Data_Binding/Transform_and_Map_Values.html): Convert a bound value to another type, scale it with gain and offset, invert it, or map it to display text, with complete dashboard YAML examples.
- [Frequently asked questions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/FAQ.html): Get short answers to common questions about building Profinity dashboards, binding tags, using profile assets and fixing problems, with links to the full pages.
- [Motor controller dashboard example](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Motor_Controller_Dashboard_Example.html): Study a complete WaveSculptor22 motor controller dashboard, section by section, with its tags and YAML, and adapt it to another controller.
- [Store dashboard files in a profile](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Store_Dashboard_Files.html): Find where to store dashboard images, 3D models, stylesheets, and content files in a profile, how YAML refers to them, and what the other directories hold.
- [Troubleshooting guide](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Troubleshooting.html): Diagnose and fix dashboard problems by symptom: data that does not update, logged data, blank charts, slow dashboards and component faults.
- [Dashboard visual editor](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Customising_Profinity/Dashboards/Visual_Editor.html): Build and change Profinity dashboards in the visual editor: add widgets, arrange them, bind tags, and save, with the YAML tab as a fallback.

- [Integrating to Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Integrating_to_Profinity/index.html): Connect other systems, applications, and AI assistants to Profinity using its REST APIs and MCP server.
- [MCP Server](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Integrating_to_Profinity/MCP_Server/index.html): Enable the Profinity MCP server and connect an AI assistant or MCP client to query live tags, history, and alerts, with permissions and troubleshooting.
- [Endpoint Reference](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Integrating_to_Profinity/APIs/Endpoint_Reference.html): Look up REST API routes for alerts, collections, derived tags, Profinity AI chat, component security, account resets, tag relay and themes.
- [Make your first API call](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Integrating_to_Profinity/First_API_Call.html): Authenticate to the Profinity REST API, then use the returned Bearer token to request the latest sample of a tag from a command line.
- [MCP tool reference](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Integrating_to_Profinity/MCP_Server/Tool_Reference.html): Look up the parameters and return values of the ten read-only tools the Profinity MCP server provides for tags, tag history and alerts.

## Developing with Profinity

- [Custom Components](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/index.html): Choose among a Dashboard Component, Custom Component, packed Custom Component, and C# plugin, then look up the files.
- [Developing with Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/index.html): Choose between scripting, Custom Components, and the Profinity SDK, including developing plugins, to extend Profinity with code.
- [Profinity Scripting](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/index.html): Automate Profinity with C#, Python, and Lua scripts: enable scripting, pick a script type and language, and find the built-in operations.
- [Supported operations](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/index.html): Look up what a script can do through the Profinity object: CAN bus, DBC, state, tags, console output, component settings and the firmware action context.
- [Script types](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/index.html): Choose between the seven Profinity script modes, including the shape a Custom Component script uses.
- [Supported Languages](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Supported_Languages/index.html): Compare C#, Python (IronPython), and Lua (NLua) for Profinity scripts, including each language's limits and .NET access.
- [Profinity SDK](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/SDK/index.html): The Profinity SDK is a developer kit Prohelion provides to approved developers, with frameworks for plugins, Custom Components, and scripts.
- [Component metadata](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Component_Metadata.html): Look up the keys of component_metadata.yaml, which names a Custom Component in the catalogue and binds the files in the folder.
- [DBC, dashboard, and rules](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/DBC_Dashboard_and_Rules.html): Attach a DBC file, a dashboard, and a rules file to a Custom Component, and bind the dashboard to its tags.
- [Custom Component files](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Files.html): Look up every file a Custom Component can include, which ones a pack requires, and which upload field holds each file.
- [Firmware actions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Firmware_Actions.html): Name the load, save, and extra firmware scripts, and the buttons those scripts put on the firmware page.
- [Firmware maps](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Firmware_Maps.html): Look up firmware_map.yaml, the firmware fields on a Custom Component, which use the same layout as a settings map.
- [Make your first Custom Component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/First_Custom_Component.html): Add a Custom Component with a dashboard, main script, menu actions, and optional DBC and firmware files.
- [Main script](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Main_Script.html): Publish live tags from a Custom Component main script, started on profile load or from Connect / Disconnect.
- [Menu actions](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Menu_Actions.html): Declare Custom Component menu actions in actions.yaml: a button, a service toggle, or Connect / Disconnect.
- [Settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Custom_Components/Settings.html): Look up the keys, field types, and layout of settings_map.yaml, the extra fields on a Custom Component settings dialog.
- [Script examples](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Examples.html): Worked C# and Python examples that read a DBC signal, send a CAN message, and keep a run count in script state, using the Example Profile.
- [Action context](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/Action.html): Read the firmware action that started a script, including the uploaded file and the invoker, and report progress back to the action.
- [CAN bus](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/CANBus.html): Send CAN packets, read the latest received packets and look packets up by CAN ID from a Profinity script in C#, Python or Lua.
- [Console](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/Console.html): Write standard and error output from a Profinity script, and find out when that output reaches the Profinity log.
- [DBC](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/DBC.html): Read signal definitions and current physical values from a loaded DBC file in a Profinity script by component, message, and signal name.
- [Component and firmware settings](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/Settings.html): Read and write a Custom Component's settings and firmware values from a script, using the field identifiers in its map files.
- [State](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/State.html): Keep values between runs of one script with State, or share them between scripts with GlobalState, in C#, Python and Lua.
- [Tags](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Operations/Tags.html): Read, write, and describe tags from a Profinity script, and learn how relative and root tag paths resolve in C#, Python and Lua.
- [Receive scripts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/Receive_Scripts.html): Run a script each time a matching CAN packet arrives, choose which packets reach it, and keep the handler fast.
- [Rule scripts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/Rule_Scripts.html): Run a script when a tag rule fires by setting Script Mode to Run On Alert, and read the alert context the rule passes to it.
- [Run scripts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/Run_Scripts.html): Run a script on demand, at a fixed interval or on a Quartz cron schedule, and learn how a Run script reports success or failure.
- [Service scripts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/Service_Scripts.html): Run continuous, long-running work with a start, stop, pause, and continue lifecycle, and learn which methods a service script must implement.
- [Tag change scripts](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/Scripting/Script_Types/Tag_Change_Scripts.html): Run a script each time a watched tag changes, choose the tags to watch, and publish computed tags without polling.
- [Component Pack CLI](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/SDK/Component_Pack_CLI.html): Validate, pack, and install Custom Component bundles with profinity-component-pack, with every command, flag, and validation rule.
- [Developing Plugins](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/SDK/Developing_Plugins.html): A plugin adds a compiled component, built on the same framework as Prohelion's own components.
- [Test a script outside Profinity](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Developing_with_Profinity/SDK/Test_a_Script.html): Create a script with profinity-script, run it on a simulated Profinity, and copy the file into a profile.

- [Troubleshoot Profinity Mobile](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Mobile/Troubleshoot_Profinity_Mobile.html): Fix an empty server list, Docker discovery, emulator, certificate warning, and single sign-on problems in the Profinity Mobile app.

## Profinity AI

- [Profinity AI](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Profinity_AI/index.html): Learn how Profinity AI uses the context of your whole Profile, through AI Chat inside Profinity and AI Skills in your own AI tool, and choose between them.
- [AI Chat](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Profinity_AI/AI_Chat.html): Open AI Chat in Profinity to ask about the live state of your instance, search the documentation, and understand its errors and limitations.
- [AI Skills reference](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Profinity_AI/AI_Skills_Reference.html): Look up the seven AI Skills, the licence, permissions, and API access they need, and what each supported AI tool can do with them.
- [AI Skills](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Profinity_AI/AI_Skills.html): Learn how AI Skills lets Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or ChatGPT build Profinity dashboards, rules, and scripts from your live instance, and when to use it.
- [Install AI Skills](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Profinity_AI/Install_AI_Skills.html): Install the Profinity AI Skills pack into Claude Code, Cursor, or Codex with npx, or set up a ChatGPT Custom GPT from the same files.

## How To Guides

- [How to guides](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/index.html): Find a Profinity 2.3 guide for building dashboards, adding components, connecting CAN bus, logging data, setting up a kiosk, connecting AI, and scripting.
- [How to add a component to your profile](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Add_Component_to_Profile.html): Add a CAN bus device, adapter, logger, or other component to the active Profinity profile, check its status colour, connect it, and remove it.
- [How to add images to your dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Add_Images_to_Dashboard.html): Add SVG, PNG, JPG, WEBP, or GIF images to a Profinity dashboard by placing them in the images folder of the profile directory and referencing them by name.
- [How to configure data logging](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Configure_Data_Logging.html): Send CAN bus messages or tag values to files, InfluxDB, Prometheus, an MQTT broker or a webhook, and check that data is flowing.
- [How to connect Profinity to AI tools like Claude or ChatGPT](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Connect_Profinity_to_AI.html): Connect an AI tool or MCP client to Profinity by enabling the MCP server, creating a service account token, and adding the server to the tool.
- [How to connect to CAN bus](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Connect_to_CAN_Bus.html): Connect Profinity to a CAN bus network with a Peak USB, SocketCAN, Ewert Energy CANdapter, or Prohelion or Tritium CAN to Ethernet bridge adapter.
- [How to create a Custom Component](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Create_Custom_Component.html): Create a new Custom Component in the active profile, then attach an optional dashboard, main script, actions, or DBC file.
- [How to create a custom dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Create_Custom_Dashboard.html): Build a dashboard for a Dashboard Component or a Custom Component in the Visual Editor, bind tags to show live data, and use the YAML tab as an alternative.
- [How to create a new profile](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Create_New_Profile.html): Create a Profinity profile for a site, location, or test setup, then activate it and add components to it.
- [How to create a profile dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Create_Profile_Dashboard.html): Replace the default Profinity home page with a custom profile dashboard, built in the visual editor or uploaded as a YAML file, and remove it again.
- [How to debug dashboard issues](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Debug_Dashboard_Issues.html): Find the cause of a dashboard that does not load, a readout with no data, a missing image, or a style that has no effect, and the usual fix for each.
- [How to log data to the cloud (InfluxDB)](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Log_Data_to_Cloud_Influx.html): Log CAN bus tag values to InfluxDB Cloud or a self-hosted InfluxDB with the InfluxDB v2 Historian, then verify the data and read its structure.
- [How to replay CAN bus logs](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Replay_CAN_Logs.html): Replay recorded CAN bus messages from a log file to test dashboards, rules, and components in Profinity without live CAN hardware.
- [How to send and receive CAN bus messages](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Send_Receive_CAN_Bus.html): Use the Profinity CAN tools to view traffic on the bus, send a CAN packet once, and schedule packets to send at an interval.
- [How to set up Profinity as a kiosk application](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Set_Up_Profinity_as_Kiosk.html): Configure Kiosk Mode in Profinity and start a fullscreen browser on Windows, Linux, or macOS so a display shows a profile without a login page.
- [How to style your dashboard](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Style_Dashboard.html): Add a profile.css stylesheet to a profile and apply its classes to dashboard groups and readouts for branding and visual customisation.
- [How to view dashboard source](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/View_Dashboard_Source.html): Open the YAML source of a component or profile dashboard in the dashboard editor, then copy it to learn from it or reuse it as a template.
- [How to write your first script](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/How_To_Guides/Write_Your_First_Script.html): Enable scripting, add a script component, and run a first C# or Python script, then find its output in the log.

## Release Notes

- [Release notes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Release_Notes/index.html): Find the release notes for Profinity 2.3.2, 2.3.1 and 2.2.5, with new features, breaking changes and upgrade information.
- [Profinity 2.2.5 release notes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Release_Notes/2.2.5.html): Release notes for Profinity 2.2.5 covering artefact directory migration, dashboard validation, CAN adapter reliability, and BMS updates.
- [Profinity 2.3 release notes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Release_Notes/2.3.1.html): Release notes for Profinity 2.3: editions and licensing, Profinity AI, derived tags, role-based security, REST error changes, and upgrading from 2.2.
- [Profinity 2.3.2 release notes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Release_Notes/2.3.2.html): Release notes for Profinity 2.3.2: stale tags, quality in logs, component visibility, theme logos, and dashboard colours.
- [Profinity 2.3 breaking changes](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Release_Notes/Breaking_Changes_2_3.html): Check what Profinity 2.3 changes for existing installations, integrations, and plugins: security files, licensing, REST API errors, data locations and defaults.

## Overview

- [Prohelion Profinity 2.3](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/index.html): Profinity 2.3 is a CAN bus and industrial data management platform that connects equipment and vehicles to AI tools, cloud services, APIs, and analytics.
- [Licensing](https://docs.prohelion.com/Profinity_Software/Profinity_Version_2.3/Licensing.html): Find which features each Profinity edition includes, how licence and site settings combine, and how the 14-day trial and machine fingerprint work.
